items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: One day Mary Holley called me.

ctx.x: You drove – you said you already drove your car there, 1960.

Yep. 1960. They had the biggest snow storm, like the recent one they had in New York. Biggest snow storm. My car is parked in front of my rooming house. A tractor comes along and tears off part of the fender. I eventually took it out to Ozone Park, Queens, which is near the – now known as the Kennedy Airport. I parked it out there one day, because it had some – actually, one of Joe Sample’s relatives I had met in L.A. prior to even going to New York. They let me park my car in front of their house, because there…

lady. Mary Holley called me. “Hubert, did you have somebody come pick up your car?” I said no. Somebody stole my car. That was the last I heard of that ’50 Plymouth. I’m going to tell you, I got a bunch of cars right now. In that garage right there, I got 1 2 3 4 5, and a truck. You know why? It’s not because I want to accumulate cars. They serve for nostalgic purposes. Each car reminds me of a certain period of my life. I got an old Porsche, right now. I just drove it back when I came back. I bought it in ’71.…
